messages.author: 0ed38b85fb72d2b8
messages.subject: Setting RHadoop enviroment on Windows 7 32bit
parts:
I tried to set up RHadoop on Windows 7 32bit. I followed http://www.srccodes.com/p/article/38/build-install-configure-run-apache-hadoop-2.2.0-microsoft-windows-os and http://bfeinsilver.blogspot.com/2014/03/installing-apache-hadoop-220-on-windows.html?showComment=1416728631354#c845587778124107742 to install Hadoop 2.2.0. Hadoop works properly (since I able to run wordcount sample).

Then I tried to run R job on Hadoop, follows http://www.rdatamining.com/big-data/r-hadoop-setup-guide.
But, I encountered an error. This is my R script.

> Sys.setenv("HADOOP_PREFIX"="C:/hadoop")
> Sys.setenv("HADOOP_CMD"="C:/hadoop/bin/hadoop")
> Sys.setenv("HADOOP_STREAMING"="C:/hadoop/share/hadoop/tools/lib/hadoop-streaming-2.2.0.jar")
> 
> library(rmr2)
> 
> ## map function
> map <- function(k,lines) {
+   words.list <- strsplit(lines, '\\s') 
+   words <- unlist(words.list)
+   return( keyval(words, 1) )
+ }
> 
> ## reduce function
> reduce <- function(word, counts) { 
+   keyval(word, sum(counts))
+ }
> 
> wordcount <- function (input, output=NULL) { 
+   mapreduce(input=input, output=output, input.format="text", 
+             map=map, reduce=reduce)
+ }
> 
> ## Submit job
> hdfs.root <- 'wordcount'
> hdfs.data <- file.path(hdfs.root, 'data') 
> hdfs.out <- file.path(hdfs.root, 'out') 
> out <- wordcount(hdfs.data, hdfs.out)
The system cannot find the batch label specified - make_command_arguments
RunJar jarFile [mainClass] args...

Could anyone please how to fix this? Any advises are appreciated.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1771] Setting RHadoop enviroment on Windows 7 32bit
parts:
It's great to have the community provide use cases and detailed installation instructions for different platforms, but not everybody is committed to updating them forever and ever. It's a problem but it's also understandable. So the first check would be making sure that those instructions are up to date and specific to your platform (hint, they aren't since they are for OS X and you have windows). The other suggestion I have to is to reach out to the author of the instructions, he or she doesn't have to do support, but may be able to at least tell you if the instructions are up to date.


Antonio
